answer: Each agent must earn a slowly released, nontransferable reputation by completing tasks that independent peers verify, with disputes checked against signed work histories. A new identity starts with no standing, so splitting one account into a hundred does not multiply influence: each must separately spend time and resources building a record. A beacon can flag suspicious clusters, while reviewers compare patterns across dune and knoll task groups; the attacker pays the full cost of credible work for every persona.
